nyciml-2012-13-spring-junior-02.title: Remove a similar pyramid
nyciml-2012-13-spring-junior-02.body:
The base has area $\frac{\sqrt3}{4}\cdot 4^2 = 4\sqrt3$, so the pyramid has volume $\frac13\cdot4\sqrt3\cdot6 = 8\sqrt3$. The plane through the midpoints of the three lateral edges cuts off a smaller pyramid similar to the original with ratio $\frac12$, so its volume is $\left(\frac12\right)^3 \cdot 8\sqrt3 = \sqrt3$. The larger solid (the frustum) has volume $8\sqrt3 - \sqrt3 = 7\sqrt3$.

**Answer: $7\sqrt3$**

nyciml-2012-13-spring-junior-03.title: Vertex of a parabola
nyciml-2012-13-spring-junior-03.body:
$xy = (6-2y)y = -2y^2+6y$, a downward parabola with vertex at $y = \frac{6}{4} = \frac32$. Then $x = 3$ and $xy = \frac92$.

**Answer: $\frac92$**

nyciml-2012-13-spring-junior-03.title: AM-GM
nyciml-2012-13-spring-junior-03.body:
$3 = \frac{x+2y}{2} \ge \sqrt{2xy}$, so $2xy\le 9$ and $xy\le\frac92$, with equality when $x = 2y$, i.e. $x=3$, $y=\frac32$.

**Answer: $\frac92$**

nyciml-2012-13-spring-junior-04.title: Add 1 and factor
nyciml-2012-13-spring-junior-04.body:
Adding $1$ to both sides gives $(x+1)(y+1)(z+1) = 385 = 5\cdot7\cdot11$. Each factor is at least $2$, and $385$ has exactly three prime factors, so $\{x+1,y+1,z+1\} = \{5,7,11\}$. With $x<y<z$: $(x,y,z) = (4,6,10)$.

**Answer: $(4, 6, 10)$**

nyciml-2012-13-spring-junior-05.title: Angle Bisector Theorem
nyciml-2012-13-spring-junior-05.body:
Let $DM = x$, so $BC = 16x$ and $BM = MC = 8x$. By the Angle Bisector Theorem $\frac{BD}{DC} = \frac{AB}{AC} < 1$, so $D$ is between $B$ and $M$: $BD = 7x$, $DC = 9x$. Hence $\frac{AB}{AC} = \frac79$.

**Answer: $\frac79$**

nyciml-2012-13-spring-junior-06.title: By group sizes
nyciml-2012-13-spring-junior-06.body:
The sizes are $3,1,1,1$ or $2,2,1,1$.
- $3,1,1,1$: choose the group of three, $\binom63 = 20$ ways.
- $2,2,1,1$: choose two unordered pairs, $\frac12\binom62\binom42 = \frac12\cdot15\cdot6 = 45$ ways.

Total $20+45 = 65$.

**Answer: 65**

nyciml-2012-13-spring-junior-06.title: Stirling recursion
nyciml-2012-13-spring-junior-06.body:
Let $S(n,k)$ count divisions of $n$ people into $k$ nonempty unlabeled groups. Person $n$ is either alone or joins one of the $k$ groups of the others: $S(n,k) = S(n-1,k-1) + k\,S(n-1,k)$. From $S(4,3)=6$, $S(4,4) = 1$, $S(4,2) = 7$: $S(5,4) = 6 + 4 = 10$, $S(5,3) = 7+3\cdot6 = 25$, and $S(6,4) = S(5,3) + 4S(5,4) = 25+40 = 65$.

**Answer: 65**

nyciml-2012-13-spring-junior-07.title: Largest numerator, smallest denominator
nyciml-2012-13-spring-junior-07.body:
The fraction is largest when the numerator is as large as possible and the denominator as small as possible, and these use different elements: $a+b = 99+98 = 197$ and $c+d = 91+92 = 183$. So the maximum is $\frac{197}{183}$.

**Answer: $\frac{197}{183}$**

nyciml-2012-13-spring-junior-08.title: By how many of the repeated color
nyciml-2012-13-spring-junior-08.body:
Let $k$ ($0\le k\le4$) be the number of balls taken of the repeated color; the other $4-k$ are distinct colors from the nine. That gives
$$\binom90+\binom91+\binom92+\binom93+\binom94 = 1+9+36+84+126 = 256.$$
(By symmetry this is half of $\sum_{j=0}^9\binom9j = 2^9$.)

**Answer: 256**

nyciml-2012-13-spring-junior-09.title: Multiples of 25
nyciml-2012-13-spring-junior-09.body:
The number is a multiple of $25$, so it ends in $00, 25, 50, 75$, and its digit sum is at most $27$, so it is at most $675$. Checking $n = 25s$ for digit sums $s = 4,\dots,27$ against the actual digit sum of $25s$ leaves exactly $s = 6, 9, 15$: $150$, $225$, $375$.

**Answer: 150, 225, 375**

nyciml-2012-13-spring-junior-10.title: Right triangle from the center
nyciml-2012-13-spring-junior-10.body:
The orange is $12$ tall, so the cut is $3$ above the table, i.e. $3$ below the center $O$. Let $P$ be the center of the cut circle and $A$ a point on its edge. Triangle $OPA$ is right with $OP = 3$ and $OA = 6$, so $PA^2 = 36-9 = 27$. The exposed area is $27\pi$.

**Answer: $27\pi$**

nyciml-2012-13-spring-junior-11.title: Scale a 30-60-90 triangle
nyciml-2012-13-spring-junior-11.body:
Let $BC = s$ (opposite the $30^\circ$ angle). Then $AC = s\sqrt3$ and $AB = 2s$, so $s(3+\sqrt3) = 3-\sqrt3$ and
$$s = \frac{3-\sqrt3}{3+\sqrt3} = \frac{(3-\sqrt3)^2}{6} = 2-\sqrt3.$$
Thus $AC = \sqrt3(2-\sqrt3) = 2\sqrt3-3$.

**Answer: $2\sqrt3-3$**

nyciml-2012-13-spring-junior-12.title: Difference of squares
nyciml-2012-13-spring-junior-12.body:
$x^4-2x^2+1 = 8x^2$, so $(x^2-1)^2 = (2\sqrt2\,x)^2$ and $x^2 - 1 = \pm 2\sqrt2\, x$. The quadratic formula gives $x = \sqrt2\pm\sqrt3$ and $x = -\sqrt2\pm\sqrt3$. The greatest is $\sqrt2+\sqrt3$.

**Answer: $\sqrt2+\sqrt3$**

nyciml-2012-13-spring-junior-13.title: Equal absolute values
nyciml-2012-13-spring-junior-13.body:
Over the reals, $u^4 = v^4$ means $u = \pm v$. $x-10 = x+6$ is impossible, and $x - 10 = -(x+6)$ gives $x = 2$.

**Answer: 2**

nyciml-2012-13-spring-junior-13.title: Equidistant point
nyciml-2012-13-spring-junior-13.body:
$|x-10| = |x+6|$ says $x$ is equally far from $10$ and $-6$, so $x$ is their midpoint, $2$.

**Answer: 2**

nyciml-2012-13-spring-junior-14.title: Double the median
nyciml-2012-13-spring-junior-14.body:
Extend $\overline{CM}$ past $M$ to $D$ with $MD = CM$. Then $ACBD$ is a parallelogram, so $CD = 2CM$ and $AD = BC = 29$. The triangle inequality in triangle $ACD$ gives $29-21 < 2CM < 29+21$, so $4 < CM < 25$. Every value in between is attained, so the integers $5,\dots,24$ give $20$ values.

**Answer: 20**

nyciml-2012-13-spring-junior-15.title: Ordered then unordered
nyciml-2012-13-spring-junior-15.body:
Pick the first square in $100$ ways; the second avoids its row and column, $81$ ways. Each set is counted twice, so there are $\frac{100\cdot81}{2} = 4050$.

**Answer: 4050**

nyciml-2012-13-spring-junior-15.title: Choose rows and columns
nyciml-2012-13-spring-junior-15.body:
Choose two rows ($\binom{10}{2} = 45$) and two columns ($45$); the two squares are one of the $2$ diagonals of the resulting $2\times2$ pattern. Total $45\cdot45\cdot2 = 4050$.

**Answer: 4050**

nyciml-2012-13-spring-junior-17.title: Area two ways
nyciml-2012-13-spring-junior-17.body:
Here $E$ is on side $\overline{AB}$ and $F$ on side $\overline{BC}$. The area is $AB\cdot DE = 6\cdot 4 = 24$, and also $BC\cdot DF = 8\,DF$, so $DF = 3$. In right triangle $CFD$, $CD = 6$, so $CF = \sqrt{36-9} = 3\sqrt3$. Since $F$ is on segment $BC$, $BF = 8-3\sqrt3$.

**Answer: $8-3\sqrt3$**

nyciml-2012-13-spring-junior-17.title: Similar triangles
nyciml-2012-13-spring-junior-17.body:
Angles $A$ and $C$ of the parallelogram are equal, so right triangles $AED$ and $CFD$ are similar: $\frac{AD}{CD} = \frac{DE}{DF}$, i.e. $\frac86 = \frac4{DF}$, so $DF = 3$. Then $CF = \sqrt{6^2-3^2} = 3\sqrt3$ and $BF = 8-3\sqrt3$.

**Answer: $8-3\sqrt3$**

nyciml-2012-13-spring-junior-18.title: Tilted plane through the same center
nyciml-2012-13-spring-junior-18.body:
The water is $\frac34\cdot3 = \frac94$ deep. Tilting keeps the volume, so the water surface is a plane through the point $O$ of the axis at height $\frac94$ (half the water gained on one side is lost on the other). Its highest point $A$ is on the rim, at height $3$, so it rises $\frac34$ over a horizontal distance of $1$ (the radius). Let $B$ be the point at height $\frac94$ directly below $A$. Then $OB = 1$, $AB = \frac34$, and $OA = \sqrt{1+\frac9{16}} = \frac54$ is the semi-major axis. The minor axis is a diameter of the glass, so the semi-minor axis is $1$. The ratio is $\frac54$. (The lowest point of the surface is at height $\frac32 > 0$, so the surface is a full ellipse.)

**Answer: $\frac54$**
